checks.name: Single source
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat single_source; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat generated_from_the_registry; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --doc compat; rustc --edition 2024 --extern automonique_protocol=rust/target/debug/libautomonique_protocol.rlib -L rust/target/debug/deps <a file naming LegacyName::LEGACY_RUNNER> and <the same file naming LegacyName::LEGACY_RUNNER_OLD>
checks.output: 9 tests pass (3 single_source, 6 generated_from_the_registry) plus 2 doctests. Something real is now generated from the registry and checked for drift. automonique_registry() declares 4 entries, 8 spellings and 4 aliases (printed by the_declared_registry_is_accepted_by_its_own_rules: "one-owner table: 4 entries, 8 spellings, 4 aliases"): AUTOMONIQUE_RUNNER/LEGACY_RUNNER, automonique doctor/legacyctl, automonique audit/legacy:audit, automonique-shell/legacy-shell, every alias citing docs/product-plan/reference/migration-plan.md, which names each of those four compatibility surfaces. emit_registry_module turns that registry into the checked-in rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/compat/generated.rs (161 lines, one constant per spelling), and the_checked_in_module_is_what_the_registry_generates compares the file against a fresh generation and names the first differing line. Negative control A (hand-written alias in the generated file): adding `pub const LEGACY_RUNNER_OLD: Self = Self(0);` to generated.rs by hand gave 22 passed / 1 failed with `line 99: checked in "    /// A hand-written alias that no registry entry declares.", registry generates "    /// The legacy alias spelled `legacy:audit`."`; removing it gave 23 passed / 0 failed. Negative control B (registry changed without regenerating): changing one entry's owner from automonique-cli to automonique-doctor-service gave 21 passed / 2 failed with `line 69: checked in "            1 => \"automonique-cli\",", registry generates "            1 => \"automonique-doctor-service\","`; restoring gave 23 passed. The compile-time half is the paired doctests on automonique_registry (src/compat.rs line 618 pass, line 632 compile_fail, both reported ok by cargo test --doc), verified standalone with rustc against libautomonique_protocol.rlib: the file naming LegacyName::LEGACY_RUNNER compiles and exits 0; the file naming LegacyName::LEGACY_RUNNER_OLD exits 1 with error[E0599] "no associated item named `LEGACY_RUNNER_OLD` found for struct `LegacyName` in the current scope". The two files differ only in the constant name. Boundary, stated rather than implied: there is still no build script anywhere in the workspace and none was added, because no Cargo.toml may be edited. "Fails the build" is therefore enforced three ways and not by build.rs — rustc refuses code naming an undeclared constant (E0599), cargo test refuses a checked-in artifact that differs from the registry, and plan/check.py refuses a hand-written LEGACY_* spelling in shipped Rust source. The E0599 half bites only code that goes through the generated constants; a bare string literal is caught by the third mechanism, not the first.

checks.name: Forwarding only
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat forwarding_only; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat the_generated_constants_and_the_registry
checks.output: 2 tests pass in forwarding_only, and 1 more now covers the real registry. Resolving AUTOMONIQUE_DB yields SpellingResolution::Canonical and resolving LEGACY_DB yields SpellingResolution::Alias, and both hand back the same NameEntry: identical canonical(), owner() and durable_identity(). An unknown spelling yields SpellingResolution::Unknown. LegacyAlias has exactly three fields (spelling, authorized_by, retire_after) and no behavior-carrying field or method, so an alias can only forward; a codec boundary is permitted by the contract but none is represented here, which is consistent with "forwarding or codec". New in this slice: the generated LegacyName carries no behavior of its own either — its only accessors are spelling, canonical, authorized_by and retire_after — and the_generated_constants_and_the_registry_name_the_same_spellings asserts for all 4 production aliases that alias.canonical().spelling(), .owner() and .durable_identity() equal what the registry resolves the alias to, so the generated forwarding table cannot claim a different owner from the registry.

checks.name: Conflict rejection
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat conflict_rejection
checks.output: 3 tests pass. Setting AUTOMONIQUE_DB=/new and LEGACY_DB=/old returns CompatError::CanonicalAndAliasBothSet naming both spellings and both values; the rendered message contains /new, /old and the word "precedence". Reversing declaration order gives the same category and still names both values. Two identical values under both spellings are still an error, so agreeing by accident is not tolerated. resolve_configuration has no precedence branch: every duplicate canonical target returns Err. Unchanged by this slice; re-measured at this base.

checks.name: Deprecation observation
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat deprecation_observation
checks.output: 2 tests pass. Setting only LEGACY_DB=/old succeeds and returns one row (canonical AUTOMONIQUE_DB, value /old) carrying Some(DeprecationObservation) whose alias()=LEGACY_DB, canonical()=AUTOMONIQUE_DB and retire_after()=0.9.0. The observation is a returned value in the Vec, not a log line, so a caller can enumerate every alias still in use. Setting only the canonical spelling returns None for the observation. Unchanged by this slice; re-measured at this base.

checks.name: One owner
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat one_owner; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat the_declared_registry -- --nocapture
checks.output: 2 tests pass in one_owner and 1 more covers the real registry. On the fixture: owner_table() emits one row per spelling (2 rows, sorted by spelling), every row agrees on owner and durable_identity, and exactly one row is flagged canonical. Inserting a second NameEntry with canonical AUTOMONIQUE_DB and owner "another-service" is refused with CompatError::TwoOwners{canonical, first: settings-service, second: another-service}. The scale caveat recorded by the previous audit is now gone: a production registry exists, and the_declared_registry_is_accepted_by_its_own_rules prints "one-owner table: 4 entries, 8 spellings, 4 aliases", asserts the table has exactly one row per spelling (8 = 4 canonical + 4 aliases, so no spelling can be missing from the proof), and asserts for every row that the owner and durable identity equal what the registry resolves that spelling to. A two-owner entry still fails at insert, which is what makes the table's agreement structural rather than coincidental.

checks.name: Authorized aliases
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat authorized_aliases; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test compat the_declared_registry
checks.output: 2 tests pass in authorized_aliases, and the_declared_registry_is_accepted_by_its_own_rules asserts a non-empty contract and a non-empty window for every alias in the production registry. The fixture alias reports authorized_by()="plan/contracts/R1-17.md" and retire_after()="0.9.0". An unauthorized alias cannot be built: MigrationContract::new("") is an error, and since LegacyAlias::new takes a MigrationContract by value there is no way to construct an alias without one. LegacyAlias::new("", ...) and LegacyAlias::new("LEGACY_DB", contract, "") are also errors. Counts for the record, now over a real registry: 4 aliases declared, 4 with an authorizing contract (all naming docs/product-plan/reference/migration-plan.md, which is the document that names each of those four compatibility surfaces), 0 without, and each with the window 0.9.0. The generated module carries both facts per alias, so authorized_by() and retire_after() are readable without running anything.

checks.name: Identifier location
checks.command: python3 plan/check.py --verify; then with tools/legacy-location-negative-control.md containing the predecessor prefix and rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/negative_control_scratch.rs containing a hand-written "LEGACY_SPOOL_ROOT" literal, the same command; then with those two files deleted; then with the fingerprint digest replaced by zeroes; then with the registry's LEGACY_RUNNER alias respelled legacy-runner and regenerated
checks.output: The enforcement exists now and is negative-controlled. plan/check.py gained check_legacy_identifier_location, called from main() alongside check_authority and check_source_licences, which walks every text file in the tree (390 files, 6.2 MB, minus .git and target) in 0.49 s and applies two rules. Rule 1: the predecessor system's identifier prefix, matched by sha256 fingerprint over lowercased word tokens of the declared length, so plan/check.py does not itself become a place the identifier appears and no failure message prints the value. Permitted in exactly four files, each with its authority recorded in LEGACY_IDENTIFIER_HOMES: docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md, rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/compat.rs, src/compat/generated.rs, and plan/gates.md — the last because the location rule's own text quotes its example, a pre-existing occurrence this item cannot edit (plan/gates.md is outside the lease) and would otherwise have to fail on. Rule 2: a "LEGACY_*" string literal in shipped Rust source (rust/crates/*/src/) outside the registry and its generated module is a hand-written alias with no authorizing entry. Measured: python3 plan/check.py --verify exits 0 with 1 warning (5 frozen harness contracts) and 0 failures. Negative control: planting the prefix in tools/legacy-location-negative-control.md and a `pub const HAND_WRITTEN: &str = "LEGACY_SPOOL_ROOT";` in rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/negative_control_scratch.rs gave exit 1 with exactly 2 failures, one per rule, each naming file and line — "tools/legacy-location-negative-control.md:4 names a legacy identifier (the predecessor system's identifier prefix); it is permitted only in ..." and "rust/crates/automonique-protocol/src/negative_control_scratch.rs:6 writes the legacy spelling LEGACY_SPOOL_ROOT by hand ...". Deleting both files returned exit 0. Both rules are also guarded against being vacuous, and both guards were exercised: replacing the fingerprint digest with 64 zeroes gave exit 1 with "the legacy-identifier fingerprints match nothing in docs/product-plan/reference/legacy-inventory.md, so the rule proves nothing", and respelling the registry's LEGACY_RUNNER alias as legacy-runner and regenerating gave exit 1 with "src/compat/generated.rs generates no LEGACY_* spelling, so the hand-written-alias rule has nothing to be about". Both perturbations were reverted and the gate returned to exit 0. Scope, stated so the row is not read as broader than it is. What is enforced is the branded half: the predecessor system's own prefix anywhere in the tree, and the product's LEGACY_* compatibility spelling in shipped Rust source. What is not enforced here is the neutral vocabulary the inventory also lists — table names, route paths, command words, third-party variable names — because AGENTS.md explicitly permits those as structural references and Automonique legitimately reuses many of them, so a scan over them would fail on migration-plan.md and on the product's own future surfaces rather than on a leak. The lowercase legacy command and binary spellings (legacyctl, legacy-shell) are covered by the R1-19 namespace gate, which refuses any identifier segment starting with legacy unless an inventory entry names its authorizing contract. Two further limits: the scan reads working-tree file contents, not commit messages (tools/scrub/scan.py owns that half and GATE-SCRUB remains open with 0 protected rules installed), and rule 2 does not scan sdk/, tools/ or test trees, because a test legitimately constructs undeclared aliases as fixtures — tests/compat.rs still uses LEGACY_DB_OLD for exactly that.

notes: Three of the four rows this run was asked to close are closed and one is left open on purpose. Single source: the registry is no longer a value type nothing generates from. automonique_registry() declares the four compatibility surfaces migration-plan.md names, emit_registry_module generates src/compat/generated.rs from it, that file is checked in, and a hand-written spelling is refused three ways — E0599 for code naming an undeclared constant (verified standalone with rustc, paired against a positive control that differs only in the constant name), a failing drift test for a hand-edited artifact, and plan/check.py for a hand-written LEGACY_* literal in shipped source. There is still no build.rs and none was added, because no Cargo.toml may be edited; the Single source row says so explicitly rather than letting "fails the build" be read as a build script. Identifier location: plan/check.py now enforces the two-location rule for the branded legacy prefix (by fingerprint, so the check does not violate the rule it enforces) and for the product's LEGACY_* compatibility spelling in shipped Rust source, with a planted-identifier negative control in a third file and anti-vacuity guards on both halves, all four perturbations run and reverted. plan/gates.md is in the permitted set because the rule's own definition there quotes its example and that file is outside this item's lease; that is a widening of the rule as written in the contract and is recorded rather than hidden. Durable identifiers unchanged is left unmeasured and blocked on R0-13, with the exact artifact R0-13 must produce written into the row. No R0-13 work was done under this item's name and no inventory was invented; the four durable identity strings in the registry are this slice's own provisional spellings and are labelled as such. Quality passed at this base. Scope choices a reviewer should look at first. (1) The registry's owner strings name target services from migration-plan.md (automonique-runner, automonique-cli, automonique-core, automonique-shell); automonique-cli is also a real crate in this workspace. The tui surface (automonique tui / legacy-tui) was deliberately left out because the plan names no owner for it and inventing one is not measurement. (2) legacyctl, legacy-shell and legacy:audit are also listed in the R1-19 namespace inventory in src/namespace.rs. Two lists now name the same three compatibility surfaces for different gates, and the right fix is for the namespace gate's inventory to be generated from this registry — that crosses into another item's file and was not done here. It is a real finding about the graph and belongs to whoever owns the next slice of either item. (3) The generator emits rustfmt-canonical text by construction; cargo fmt --all -- --check is what keeps the two in agreement, and the one construct that could drift with registry size (the ALL array) is emitted on one line only below rustfmt's array width. A one-entry registry is handled without a match, because match self.0 { _ => x } is a single-binding match that strict Clippy refuses.
